chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Nadr, from Abu al-Husayn, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Fear Allah as He should truly be feared.' He said: 'He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not shown ingratitude.'

key_terms.حَقَّ تِقَادِهِ: As He should truly be feared (proper manner of fear)
key_terms.يُذْكَرُ فَلَا يُنْسَى: He is remembered and not forgotten
key_terms.يُشْكُرُ فَلَا يُكْفَرُ: He is thanked and not shown ingratitude
key_terms.يُطَاعُ فَلَا يُعْصَى: He is obeyed and not disobeyed

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Fear Allah as He should truly be feared' mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Quranic command to fear Allah with true fear by defining it through the triad of consistent obedience, remembrance, and gratitude. This interpretation shifts the focus from mere anxiety to a holistic state of worship where faith is sustained by avoiding its opposites: disobedience, forgetfulness, and ingratitude. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *taqwa* as an active, continuous practice of aligning one’s actions with divine will.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Nadhr, from Abul Hussain that Abu Basir said:

"I asked Abu 'Abdillah (al-Sadiq) (as) about the saying of Allah (swt): «Fear Allah how He should truly be feared» [3:102], he said: 'He should be obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not [shown] ingratitude.'"
